newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Saab new model to debut in Europe '97.
newsitem.headline: Saab new model to debut in Europe '97.

text.p: Swedish-U.S. car maker Saab Automobile AB said on Wednesday that it would introduce a new model in Europe in the autumn of 1997 and in the U.S. in the beginning of 1998.

Robert Hendry, managing director of the car maker jointly owned by Swedish investment company Investor AB and U.S. automotive group General Motors (GM), said order bookings were higher than one year ago.

"The new Saab model will be introduced in Europe in the autumn and in the U.S. at the beginning of 1998. It will be previewed to journalists during the summer this year," he told Reuters after a speech in the western Swedish city.
Saab Automobile's sales started strong in 1997, especially in Britain. The company's order bookings are higher now than they were one year ago, Hendry said.

"We have had a strong start in Britain this year... In Sweden we also began well but saw a marginal fall in the U.S. in January. But the U.S. firm stands by its forecasts for the first quarter, and this points to an increase in U.S. sales," he said.
"We have noticed increased demand in Sweden this year and our order bookings are higher now than they were one year ago," Hendry said.
The new Saab model will carry the 640 mark. Small scale production will begin at Saab's Trollhattan plant in southern Sweden.

"The production of the new model will start in a small scale on our usual production lines. The cars will be tested and go through quality control. Production will gradually increase until the car is introduced on the market," he said.
